clue.text: Boy's name put before masters this term

parts.note: a common boy's name
MA is a Master of Arts degree, so masters gives the plural

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's name goes up on the list ahead of the teachers for the new term.
explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas is the autumn term at Oxford, Cambridge and many British schools, named after the feast of St Michael on 29 September.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumn academic term in British universities and schools carries the name of the Michaelmas feast day.

clue.text: Fail to meet unmarried woman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not catch up with someone
second meaning: the title for a woman who is not married

explanation.surface: Someone stands up a single woman they were due to see.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to fail to connect with someone, and the noun is the traditional title for a woman without a husband.

clue.text: Orinoco River's burst — that could cause rusting

indicators.note: a river that has burst its banks spills everywhere, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: When the great South American river floods, the water damage could leave metal rusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S of River's is used as a letter, which is easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrosion is the chemical wearing away of metal, the process that turns iron to rust.

clue.text: He endures a wife being abroad for so long in parts of Europe

definitions.text: so long in parts of Europe

indicators.note: something abroad is all over the place, out of its usual position, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man puts up with his wife travelling overseas for a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like a length of time, but it is a farewell, and the German phrase is how you say goodbye in Germany and Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The German farewell phrase translates as goodbye until we see each other again, the counterpart of so long.

clue.text: Yearn to be on stage in cricketer's position?

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: An actor longs to be on stage, standing in their cricketing position.
explanation.walkthrough: Long leg is a fielding position in cricket, deep behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the fielders stand at named places, and this is one of them, far out on the leg side.

clue.text: Serious novelist, almost touching

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the novelist's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Jane Austen, author of Pride and Prejudice
re means concerning or touching on

explanation.surface: A grave author whose writing is nearly moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere describes a stern, severe manner, close to grave or serious in tone.

clue.text: Examine clipped earring

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed short, so the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to study is to examine closely

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a clip-on earring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped earring' looks like a clip-on, but clipped belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a small earring fixed through the lobe on a post, a common kind of ear jewellery.

clue.text: Stimulant to take (short)

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word for take loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
to nick is to take or steal

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up to be taken in a short measure, like a quick drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a medicine or drink that invigorates, so it acts as a stimulant or restorative.

clue.text: Does household chore with these spread? They may cover the furniture

parts.note: dusting is a household chore

indicators.note: spread means laid out loosely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaner dusts while these covers are spread over the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust sheets are large cloths laid over furniture to protect it while a room is shut up or decorated.

clue.text: Statesman will overcome Left, right? Wrong

indicators.note: wrong means out of the proper order, so these letters must be set right again

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A politician will defeat both left and right wings, or so he claims, wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell led the Parliamentary side in the English Civil War and ruled as Lord Protector.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell was a seventeenth-century English political and military leader, so he is an example of a statesman.

clue.text: Dismisses, on reflection, additional line in letter?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them

explanation.surface: A boss thinks again about dismissing staff over a postscript added to a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Additional line in letter' suggests a postscript, but the letter is a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small finishing stroke added at the ends of a printed character's strokes.

clue.text: Young birds in eyries fed fish?

indicators.note: something fed is given food to take inside it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an eyrie is an eagle's nest
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Baby eagles in their high nests are fed on fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestlings are chicks too young to leave the nest, a common term for young birds.

clue.text: Parties about to check welfare work

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a social is an informal party or gathering
a service is a routine check of a car or machine

explanation.surface: Political parties are about to scrutinise the welfare system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' looks political, and 'about to' looks like 'soon going to'; in fact about is split off as the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Social services are the publicly provided welfare support, such as social work and care for vulnerable people.

clue.text: Help while one's in position

parts.note: as can mean while, in 'as I was leaving'

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here within the word for position

parts.note: a stance is a position or posture
one is read as the numeral I, and the 's as is

explanation.surface: Someone helps out while a person is getting into position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'While' looks like a time word joining two clauses, but it supplies letters; 'one's' is read as one is, with one as the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is the noun for aid or support, the same as help used as a noun.

clue.text: His awful din spoiled good lively party

indicators.note: awful means bad and garbled, so these letters are put into a new order
spoiled means messed up, which extends the rearrangement to take in the last letter too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A man's dreadful racket ruined a good, lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a noisy, lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Complaint made by bridge player facing a girl that's cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the girl's name loses its final letter

parts.note: East is one of the four players at bridge, abbreviated E
taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a bridge player sitting opposite a girl who snubbed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' just places the bridge player before the rest; the four bridge seats are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an ailment, and an earache is a painful ailment of the ear.

clue.text: Set, before drop of champagne in mansion, played on this?

indicators.note: a drop is just a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the drink is used

parts.note: the first letter of champagne
to lay something down is to set it
court is a name for a grand house, as in Hampton Court

explanation.surface: A tennis set, with champagne at a grand house, played on this surface?
explanation.walkthrough: The C comes before the word for set; 'Set' looks like tennis, which is the scene, but here it means lay.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay court is a tennis court surfaced with crushed brick or clay, as at the French Open.

clue.text: Pays no attention to poor regions

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so these letters are reworked into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The government neglects deprived areas of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them deliberately, a synonym for paying them no attention.

clue.text: Some consult an astrologer for a Muslim ruler's wife perhaps

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of consult, all of an, and the start of astrologer

explanation.surface: Some people consult a stargazer about a sultan's consort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife, mother or daughter of a sultan, so a sultan's wife is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: The Queen by vehicle in street getting help

indicators.note: in places the queen and her transport inside the abbreviation for a road

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: The Queen, stuck in her car on the road, gets assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is someone employed to help in a household, a sense still used in calling domestic staff 'the help'.

clue.text: Study is over, i.e. indefinitely adjourned

indicators.note: turned over means upside down, which in a down entry reads the letters backwards

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The study is over, that is, put off with no date for resuming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is over' sounds finished, but over turns round the study and is together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for 'without a day', the formal phrase for a meeting adjourned with no date to resume.

clue.text: Children bet me I misinterpreted nursery rhyme

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so these letters are taken in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The kids wagered that I had got the words of a nursery rhyme wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known English nursery rhyme about three sightless rodents chased by a farmer's wife.

clue.text: Rook seen over river in the country

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: rural means of or in the countryside

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A rook is spotted flying over a river out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over means placed above, so the rook comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes places or life belonging to the countryside rather than the town.

clue.text: Extra de luxe? No end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter is removed from the word

parts.note: plush means luxurious

explanation.surface: An extra de luxe item that seems to have no limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' reads as 'endlessly', but it instructs a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an added benefit or bonus, and as an adjective it means additional, both senses of extra.

clue.text: Who could be a minder with us, if trained?

definitions.text: Who could be a minder with us, if trained?

indicators.note: training reshapes something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who might look after the children, if given proper training.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a trained minder living with the family is the job described.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children, a trained minder in the household.

clue.text: Like a peer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the same as, as an adjective
second meaning: a person of the same rank, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests a lord, but here it means someone of matching standing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for things that are alike and a noun for someone's counterpart or match in status.

clue.text: Girl from Israel — lawyer

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are lifted straight out of the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of Israel and the start of lawyer

explanation.surface: A young woman from Israel works as a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a female given name, so it is an example of a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Celestial bodies getting a mention in places

indicators.note: in places the first words inside the word for places

parts.note: sites are places or locations
taken as written
to tell is to mention or relate

explanation.surface: Stars and planets receive a mention in various spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellites are moons and other bodies orbiting a planet, so they are examples of objects in space.
